cohort: Singleton children from the 2015 Pelotas Birth Cohort in Brazil, aged 4 to 7 years at the time of assessment.
finding: Children aged 4 to 7 years born through planned cesarean section before labor had significantly lower hair cortisol levels compared to those born vaginally or via unplanned cesarean section after labor.
mod_finding: Children born through planned CS before labor had 6.6% lower hair cortisol than children born vaginally and 4.4% lower than children born from unplanned CS after labor, with no significant differences between children born vaginally and through CS after labor, suggesting that labor exposure (especially before 39.5 weeks gestation) is associated with the observed differences.
gest_age: Differences in hair cortisol were most pronounced among children born without labor at earlier gestational ages, with adjusted differences between planned CS and vaginal delivery significant before 39.5 weeks gestation.
